# QueryFence

> SQL policy testing for the JVM. Declare a rule once (for example: every query touching
> purchase_order must filter by tenant_id); QueryFence checks every SQL statement your integration
> tests actually send to the database, and fails the build on the ones that break the rule,
> pointing at the class, method and line that produced the query.

Status: 0.1.0, the first release. Coordinates: com.steelreed:queryfence-*:0.1.0.
Apache-2.0. Java 17+. The API is small but not frozen before 1.0.
Repository: https://github.com/steelreed/queryfence
Docs: https://steelreed.github.io/queryfence/

## What it is not

- Not a runtime guard: it never rewrites or blocks SQL. Postgres RLS, Hibernate @TenantId and
  MyBatis interceptors enforce; QueryFence verifies in tests that the SQL really carries the filter.
- Not a static analyser: it only sees SQL that tests execute.
- It does not check parameter *values*, only that a tenant predicate exists.

## Setup (Spring Boot)

1. Test-scope dependency com.steelreed:queryfence-spring-test.
2. src/test/resources/queryfence.yml (below).
Nothing else: no annotation, no change to test code. Every DataSource bean of a Spring test context
is wrapped automatically. Without Spring, use queryfence-junit5 with
`@RegisterExtension static QueryFenceExtension fence = QueryFenceExtension.fromClasspath();` and
`fence.wrap(dataSource)`.

## Policy file

```yaml
version: 1
mode: FAIL              # or REPORT (collect only)
onUnparseable: FAIL     # or REPORT; governs UNPARSEABLE findings only, not `mode`
rules:
  - id: tenant-isolation
    type: require-predicate
    column: tenant_id
    tables: [purchase_order, order_item]
    allowedFunctions: [current_setting]   # optional
    primaryKey: id                        # optional, default id
  - id: no-unbounded-update
    type: update-without-where
  - id: no-unbounded-delete
    type: delete-without-where
suppressions:
  - rule: tenant-isolation
    origin: com.acme.admin.ReportJob#nightlyTotals
    reason: Platform report, runs as the operator.   # required, non-blank
```

## Rule semantics (require-predicate)

Every occurrence of a protected table must be fenced by conditions that apply to it:
- Value predicate: `<alias>.<column> = ?`/literal/named or positional parameter/allowed function/cast.
- `<alias>.<column> IN (values)`; not IN (subquery), not NOT IN, not inequalities.
- Transitive: `i.tenant_id = o.tenant_id` fences i when o is fenced; a chain needs one value anchor.
- AND fences what any conjunct fences; OR fences only what EVERY branch fences (recursively).
- Placement: WHERE, any INNER JOIN ON, or the ON of the LEFT JOIN that introduces that table.
- Each subquery, CTE body and UNION branch is its own query block; filters outside a derived table
  or CTE do not fence what is inside it.
- INSERT: the tenant column must appear in the column list.
- Fail closed: unparseable DML, MERGE on a protected table, and unprovable statements are violations.

## Violation codes

MISSING_PREDICATE, PRIMARY_KEY_LOOKUP (only filtered by id: findById/EntityManager.find),
AMBIGUOUS_COLUMN, MISSING_INSERT_COLUMN, NO_WHERE, TAUTOLOGICAL_WHERE, UNSUPPORTED_STATEMENT,
UNPARSEABLE. Every message states the problem and the fix.

## Known conservative reports (ORM)

- findById / EntityManager.find -> PRIMARY_KEY_LOOKUP. Fix: findByIdAndTenantId, or Hibernate
  @TenantId on the entity.
- Fetch join / lazy association loads children by foreign key -> reported. Fix: map the tenant on
  the child entity (@TenantId); fallback: protect only the aggregate root (the child table is then
  not checked).
- A tenant filter applied outside a derived table or CTE does not fence what is inside it.

## Adoption path

Start with mode: REPORT, run the existing test suite, read target/queryfence/report.json, and
triage each origin into real leak / false positive / documented suppression. Then switch to FAIL.
Helper: `python3 tools/queryfence-summary.py target/queryfence/report.json --triage`.
Full guide: https://steelreed.github.io/queryfence/ADOPTION/

## Capture window

Only statements executed by the test method and the code it calls, on any thread. Fixtures in
@BeforeEach/@AfterEach, Spring context startup and migrations are outside it.

## Switching it off

queryfence.enabled=false disables the checks, prints a loud warning, writes "disabled": true into
the report and fails the build when the CI environment variable is set, unless
queryfence.allowDisabledInCi=true. Prefer a suppression with a reason.

## Modules

queryfence-core (engine, JSqlParser only), queryfence-jdbc (DataSource proxy, StackWalker origin),
queryfence-report (findings, console summary, report.json), queryfence-junit5 (extension, YAML),
queryfence-spring-test (wraps DataSource beans), queryfence-bom.
